fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run '^TestScriptOrder$' shows: given timings, scripts come in descending seconds, ties and scripts missing from the file by name, and every *.txtar exactly once; failure case: a malformed timings line (no tab, or seconds not a number) fails with the file's line number. Touches cmd/rhiza/main_test.go and a new cmd/rhiza/order_test.go. Must not change any script's content or environment.
fields.statement: TestScripts hands testscript its Files longest first by script-timings.tsv, scripts missing from the file after them by name. This orders the list only, not the start: testscript runs each script as a t.Parallel subtest, and Go hands the -parallel slots to the woken subtests in no guaranteed order, so nothing here promises that the longest scripts start first.

set.acceptance: A Go test in cmd/rhiza (go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScriptShard) asserts that for n=4 the four shards are disjoint, together cover every script in testdata/script, and are the greedy split by recorded time (each script, longest first by script-timings.tsv, to the shard with the least total so far); that unset selects all scripts; and that a malformed value (0/4, 5/4, x) fails with a clear error.
set.statement: TestScripts runs one shard of cmd/rhiza's scripts when RHIZA_TEST_SHARD=i/n is set (1-based): the scripts assigned to shard i when each, longest first by cmd/rhiza/testdata/script-timings.tsv, goes to the shard with the least recorded time so far, passed as testscript Files; unset, it runs every script, longest first (@{01M7EQE69J35XJW25SPBZBH1MS}).
